He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yakima Valley College#Athletics|Yakima Valley Yaks]]. ==High school career== Before entering high school, Beauchamp moved from his hometown of [[Yakima, Washington]], to [[Seattle]] to play basketball at [[Nathan Hale High School (Washington)|Nathan Hale High School]] under head coach [[Brandon Roy]] and to face stronger competition.{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jayda |title=With addition of five-star guard MarJon Beauchamp, Rainier Beach could be the state favorite again |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/with-addition-of-five-star-marjon-beauchamp-rainier-beach-a-state-contender-again/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=November 26, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Saez |first=Rosin |title=Meet Washington's Most Promising Basketball Star |url=https://www.seattlemet.com/articles/2019/2/19/meet-washington-s-most-promising-basketball-star |website=[[Seattle Metropolitan]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=February 19, 2019}} As a freshman, he was a deep reserve for a team that featured top recruits [[Michael Porter Jr.]] and [[Jontay Porter]].{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jayda |title=Rainier Beach five-star recruit MarJon Beauchamp is transferring to Arizona prep school |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/rainier-beachs-marjon-beauchamp-is-transferring-to-arizona-prep-school/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=June 7, 2019}} Nathan Hale finished with a 29–0 record, won the [[Washington Interscholastic Activities Association]] Class 3A state title, and captured the No. 1 national ranking from [[MaxPreps]].{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jayda |title=Nathan Hale finishes off perfect season with a flourish, beating Garfield for Class 3A state title |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/nathan-hale-finishes-off-perfect-season-with-a-flourish-beating-garfield-for-class-3a-state-title/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=March 4, 2017}}{{cite web |last=Hickman |first=Jason |title=Final 2016-17 MaxPreps High School Top 25 Boys Basketball Rankings |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/m6mNCn3U0Uq6fWdm19xzRg/final-2016-17-maxpreps-high-school-top-25-boys-basketball-rankings-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=August 4, 2019 |date=March 31, 2017}} As a sophomore, Beauchamp transferred to [[Garfield High School (Seattle)|Garfield High School]] in Seattle.{{cite web |last=Prezkop |first=Dylan |title=Player Intro: 2020 Wing MarJon Beauchamp |url=https://www.nextuprecruits.com/news_article/show/800215 |publisher=Next Up Recruits |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=June 26, 2017}} He moved to the school with former Nathan Hale coach Brandon Roy and teammate P. J. Fuller.{{cite web |last=Evans |first=Jayda |title=Boys basketball preview: Addition of P.J. Fuller makes loaded Garfield even more dangerous |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball-preview-addition-of-p-j-fuller-makes-loaded-garfield-even-more-dangerous/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=December 7, 2017}} He won his second straight Class 3A state championship and helped Garfield reach the quarterfinals at High School Nationals.{{cite web |title=No. 2 Oak Hill Academy dominates No. 12 Garfield in GEICO Nationals quarterfinals |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/mH_dU1n6WEmV2zyu0ennlw/no-2-oak-hill-academy-dominates-no-12-garfield-in-geico-nationals-quarterfinals.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=March 29, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Lommers |first=Aaron |title=Tacoma native Pierre Crockrell Jr. has breakout tournament, leads Garfield to 3A state championship |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article203413539.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=March 4, 2018}} For his junior season, Beauchamp transferred to [[Rainier Beach High School]] in Seattle, citing a lack of motivation in class and sickness from [[Mold (fungus)|mold]] in his house during his time at Garfield. He moved to the [[South End, Seattle|South End]], within school boundaries, and as a result was ruled eligible to play basketball for his new school. After leading Rainier Beach to league and district titles, he was named [[most valuable player]] of the Seattle 3A [[Metro League (Seattle)|Metro League]].{{cite web |title=Rainier Beach's Marjon Beauchamp named 2019 Metro League boys basketball MVP (Seattle All-Metro teams) |url=https://sblivewa.com/2019/02/20/rainier-beachs-marjon-beauchamp-named-2019-metro-league-boys-basketball-mvp-seattle-all-metro-teams/ |publisher=Scorebook Live Washington |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=February 20, 2019}} Beauchamp guided his team to a Class 3A state semifinal appearance and fifth place in the state tournament. He averaged 26 points, 11 rebounds, and five assists per game and was named to the ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Washington second team, [[Associated Press]] Class 3A All-State first team, and ''[[The Seattle Times]]'' All-State second team.{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA Washington Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-washington-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=April 16, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Manley |first=Jon |title=High school basketball: 2018-19 Washington AP all-state basketball teams |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article228791744.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=April 3, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Cotterill |first=TJ |title=Seattle Times All-State boys basketball team: All the winning sets Gonzaga Prep's Anton Watson apart |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/seattle-times-all-state-boys-basketball-team-all-the-winning-set-gonzaga-preps-anton-watson-apart/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=March 10, 2019}} Beauchamp transferred to Dream City Christian School, a school in [[Glendale, Arizona]] with a new basketball program, for his senior season.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=5-star SF MarJon Beauchamp transferring to Dream City Christian in Arizona |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/marjon-beauchamp-transferring-to-dream-city |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=July 15, 2019}} After finishing his high school basketball career he went back to his hometown of Yakima to graduate from Eisenhower High School. ===Recruiting=== After his freshman season, Beauchamp held offers from four [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. His success on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit helped him earn a five-star rating from recruiting websites before his junior season. Beauchamp was rated a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by major recruiting services at the end of his high school career.{{cite web |title=MarJon Beauchamp |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/231073 |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}{{cite web |title=MarJon Beauchamp, Dream City Christian, Small Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/MarJon-Beauchamp-46046880/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Marjon Beauchamp, 2020 Small forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2020/marjon-beauchamp-208339 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019}} On August 1, 2019, he announced that he would forgo [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last=Roscher |first=Liz |title=5-star prospect MarJon Beauchamp will skip college to prepare for 2021 NBA draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/5-star-prospect-mar-jon-beauchamp-will-skip-college-to-prepare-for-2021-nba-draft-163446979.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=August 5, 2019 |date=August 1, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = MarJon Beauchamp | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Yakima, WA]] | highschool = Dream City Christian (AZ) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 175 | 40 = | commitdate = — | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 87 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | 247 overall = 34 | rivals overall = 48 | espn overall = 44 | accessdate = April 29, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Following high school, Beauchamp trained with Chameleon BX, a training program based in [[San Francisco]], to prepare for the [[2021 NBA draft]]. After over six months with the program, he returned to Washington due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and began reconsidering his college options.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=Former Dream City star MarJon Beauchamp reassesses basketball future, looks to take college route |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/02/25/former-dream-city-star-marjon-beauchamp-looks-college-route/6824717002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=February 25, 2021}} In March 2021, Beauchamp joined the basketball team at [[Yakima Valley Community College]] in his hometown, being drawn by his friendship with players on the team. In his college debut on April 20, 2021, Beauchamp had nine points and nine rebounds in a 99–90 loss over [[Treasure Valley Community College|Treasure Valley]], and felt lingering respiratory limitations.{{cite web |last=Thompson |first=Luke |title=MarJon Beauchamp makes surprise homecoming, eager to take advantage of a short season at Yakima Valley |url=https://www.yakimaherald.com/sports/college_sports/yvcc_sports/marjon-beauchamp-makes-surprise-homecoming-eager-to-take-advantage-of-a-short-season-at-yakima/article_515c57c0-55e0-5f8c-bc47-aef6dbca3ab6.html |website=[[Yakima Herald-Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=April 24, 2021}} On June 1, he recorded a career-high 50 points and 11 rebounds in a 107–106 overtime loss to Treasure Valley.{{cite web |title=Local Report: Beauchamp drops 50 in Yakima Valley's OT basketball loss |url=https://www.yakimaherald.com/sports/college_sports/yvcc_sports/local-report-beauchamp-drops-50-in-yakima-valleys-ot-basketball-loss/article_ae6d6098-5684-5b70-9577-d3b052464c38.html |website=[[Yakima Herald-Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=June 1, 2021}} As a freshman, Beauchamp averaged 30.7 points, 10.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game through 12 games, leading the [[Northwest Athletic Conference]] in scoring.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Prospect MarJon Beauchamp signs with G League Ignite program |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32077536 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=August 24, 2021}}{{cite web |title=Antonio Salinas, MarJon Beauchamp invited to play in The Crawsover |url=https://www.yakimaherald.com/sports/college_sports/yvcc_sports/antonio-salinas-marjon-beauchamp-invited-to-play-in-the-crawsover/article_55c7ba28-3455-5ac7-b63a-e2db1c0211a4.html |website=[[Yakima Herald-Republic]] |access-date=August 24, 2021 |date=July 8, 2021}} He drew attention from [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]], [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] and [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], but opted to forgo attending a [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] university due to concerns about his amateur status.{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=August 25, 2021 |title=Prospect MarJon Beauchamp signs with G League Ignite program |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32077536 |access-date=August 25, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2021–2022)=== On September 23, 2021, Beauchamp signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Marjon Beauchamp Signs with NBA G League Ignite|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/marjon-beauchamp-signs-with-nba-g-league-ignite/n-5749103|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=September 23, 2021|access-date=September 25, 2021}} He averaged 15.1 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Stone |first=Larry |title=Inside the amazing, convoluted journey MarJon Beauchamp took from Yakima to the NBA draft |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/nba/inside-the-amazing-convulted-journey-marjon-beauchamp-took-from-yakima-to-the-nba-draft/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=June 22, 2022 |date=June 18, 2022}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2022–2025)=== On June 23, 2022, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] drafted Beauchamp 24th overall in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He joined the Bucks' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612749/bucks |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=nba.com}} In his Summer League debut, Beauchamp scored sixteen points in a 94–90 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets vs Milwaukee Bucks Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/bkn-vs-mil-1522200006/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=nba.com}} On July 7, 2022, Beauchamp signed a rookie-scale contract with the Bucks.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=July 7, 2022 |title=Bucks sign former Ignite guard MarJon Beauchamp to rookie contract |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/07/07/bucks-marjon-beauchamp-rookie-contract/ |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=The Rookie Wire}} On November 9, Beauchamp set a career high with 19 points scored, along with 8 rebounds grabbed, during a 136–132 win over the [[2022–23 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=November 10, 2022 |title='It was impressive': Bucks' MarJon Beauchamp puts up career high in second start |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/11/10/bucks-marjon-beauchamp-double-overtime-highlights |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=therookiewire.usatoday.com}} On November 14, Beauchamp set a new career high with 20 points during a 121–106 loss to the [[2022–23 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |last=Kleifield |first=Rob |date=November 18, 2022 |title=Buzz growing around Bucks rookie Beauchamp |url=https://www.ballysports.com/wisconsin/news/buzz-growing-around-bucks-rookie-marjon-beauchamp-nba-draft-giannis |access-date=August 6, 2023 |publisher=Bally Sports}} On 24 January 2024, playing for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]'s [[NBA G League|G-League]] affiliate team [[Wisconsin Herd]], Beauchamp scored 36 points on 13-26 shooting along with 5 rebounds and 3 assists from the field in a 107–120 win against the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{Cite web |title=BHM @ WIS, 2024-01-24 |url=https://gleague.nba.com/game/bhm-vs-wis-2022300175 |access-date=2024-01-27 |website=The NBA G League |language=en}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2025)=== On February 6, 2025, Beauchamp was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Kevin Porter Jr.]] {{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-acquire-beauchamp-from-milwaukee|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|title=Clippers Acquire Beauchamp From Milwaukee }} On March 1, Beauchamp was waived by the Clippers. {{cite web|url=https://www.rotowire.com/basketball/headlines/marjon-beauchamp-news-let-go-by-clippers-485197|work=rotowire.com|date=March 1, 2025|title= MarJon Beauchamp News: Let go by Clippers }} ===New York Knicks (2025)=== On March 4, 2025, Beauchamp signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web | last=Simon | first=Dean | title=Knicks officially sign former Bucks, Clippers forward to two-way contract | website=Sporting News | date=2025-03-03 | url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/new-york-knicks/news/knicks-officially-sign-former-bucks-clippers-forward-two-way-contract/11632e4df47f35f064ddfeab | access-date=2025-12-09}} ===Delaware Blue Coats / Philadelphia 76ers (2025–2026)=== On October 14, 2025, Beauchamp signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] following the release of [[Emoni Bates]].{{cite web |last=Carlin |first=Ky |date=October 14, 2025 |title=Sixers officially sign MarJon Beauchamp to a deal, waive Emoni Bates |website=USA Today – Sixers Wire |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/sixers/2025/10/14/sixers-officially-sign-marjon-beauchamp-to-a-deal-waive-emoni-bates/86698286007/ |access-date=November 2, 2025 }} However, four days later, Beauchamp was waived by the 76ers.{{cite web |last=RotoWire Staff |date=October 18, 2025 |title=MarJon Beauchamp: Waived by 76ers |website=CBS Sports |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/marjon-beauchamp-waived-by-76ers/ |access-date=November 2, 2025 }} On December 23, Beauchamp signed a [[two-way contract]] with the 76ers after an impressive run playing for their [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{Cite web|title=76ers sign former 1st-round pick from Bucks to new contract|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/76ers-sign-former-1st-round-151743237.html|access-date=December 24, 2025}} Beauchamp averaged over 26.5 points, seven rebounds, and three assists over five games.{{Cite web |title=Marjon Beauchamp's Statistics |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1630699/}} ===FC Bayern Munich (2026–present)=== On August 12, 2026, Beauchamp signed a one-year contract with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|FC Bayern Munich]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Bayern reels in NBA forward MarJon Beauchamp|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/bayern-reels-in-nba-forward-marjon-beauchamp/|date=August 12, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=August 12, 2026}}
